questions_and_answers.question: What does the indefinite relative pronoun 'was' introduce?

answers.answer: Relative clauses referring back to indefinite words such as alles, das, etwas and nichts
Questions about the past
Prepositional phrases
Dependent clauses introduced by dass

questions_and_answers.question: Which special combining forms does 'was' take after prepositions?

answers.answer: was- or wor-
an- or auf-
wer- or wem-
das- or dem-

questions_and_answers.question: Translate the sentence 'Nichts, was er sagte, war richtig' into English.

answers.answer: Nothing (that) he said was right
Everything he said was right
What he said was unclear
He said nothing right

questions_and_answers.question: What does 'Das ist etwas, was ich wirklich sehr empfehlen kann' mean?

answers.answer: That is something I can really recommend very highly
That is nothing I recommend
This is something I cannot recommend
This is someone I recommend

articles.text:
E. THE INDEFINITE RELATIVE PRONOUN - was
In this unit we have encountered a new type of relative clause, introduced by the pronoun was. Seitdem ich zu Hause bin, strengt mich alles, was ich tue, sehr an. Since I've been home again everything I do fatigues me very much. The INDEFINITE RELATIVE PRONOUN was introduces relative clauses referring back to the indefinite words alles, das, etwas and nichts. Nichts, was er sagte, war richtig. Das ist etwas, was ich wirklich sehr empfehlen kann. Das, was er schrieb, war sehr gut. Nothing (that) he said was right. That is something (that) I can recommend very highly. What he wrote was very good. Like the question-word was it has the special combining form was- or wor- after prepositions. Das war alles, was sie gedacht hatte. Das ist etwas, worüber man sich freuen kann. That was all that she was thinking of. That's something you can be happy about.
